reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker data available to confirm PD-L1 engagement by avelumab. The trial assumes target engagement based on the mechanism but provides no direct evidence. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pharmacodynamic markers or biomarkers reported to confirm that PD-L1 blockade led to T-cell activation or immune pathway modulation. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint (OS in PD-L1+ population) missed with HR 0.87, p=0.0721. While numerically favorable, it did not reach statistical significance. PFS also failed in both overall and PD-L1+ populations. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: PD-L1+ subgroup showed numerically better outcomes (OS 11.4 vs 10.6 months, ORR 18.9% vs 11.7%) suggesting the biomarker may identify a more responsive subset, but still failed to reach significance. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Trial appears adequately powered (n=792) with appropriate duration (202.9 weeks). Safety profile was acceptable with lower grade 3+ AEs than control (53.2% vs 67.7%).

failure_modes.evidence: PD-L1+ population showed numerically better OS and higher response rate compared to full population, suggesting some biological activity, but primary endpoint still missed statistical significance
